AHFA honors three industry leaders with Distinguished Service Awards

RANCHO MIRAGE, Calif. — The American Home Furnishings Alliance has presented its highest honor, the Distinguished Service Award, to three longtime members of its leadership team: Bill Perdue, vice president of regulatory affairs; Jackie Hirschhaut, vice president of public relations and marketing; and Patricia Bowling, vice president of communications.
With at least 25 years each at AHFA, the three were recognized November 13 during the 2026 Annual Meeting & CEO Conference in Rancho Mirage, Calif.

Established in 1966, the Distinguished Service Award recognizes individuals whose leadership, dedication and service have made a significant impact on the home furnishings industry. Perdue, Hirschhaut and Bowling join former association executives Douglas Brackett, honored in 1990, and Joseph Gerard, honored in 1999, as the only five AHFA staff members to receive the award.

“Bill, Jackie and Pat have each devoted decades of their careers to serving AHFA and the home furnishings industry,” said Andy Counts, AHFA’s CEO. “Through their leadership, expertise and dedication, they have earned the trust and respect of industry leaders, strengthened relationships and helped our members navigate challenges and opportunities. Each has made a significant impact in their own way, giving their time, talent and heart to an industry that is stronger because of their contributions.”

Bill Perdue: Advancing Regulatory Affairs and Furniture Safety
Perdue joined the American Furniture Manufacturers Association (now AHFA) in November 2001, bringing nearly two decades of experience in environmental management and regulatory compliance to the association, including 11 years as director of engineering for Pulaski Furniture.

During his 25 years with AHFA, Perdue has become a leading industry authority on environmental regulations, product safety and compliance matters. He has represented the home furnishings industry before federal and state agencies and standards organizations, advocating for practical regulatory solutions and helping shape policies affecting furniture manufacturers.

His leadership has been particularly influential in furniture safety. As a longtime participant and former chair of the ASTM International subcommittee on furniture safety, Perdue helped guide the industry through years of debate over updates to the voluntary standards for clothing storage furniture and bunk beds. In 2022, he gathered a task group of top furniture engineers and coordinated the technical research that paved the way for passage of the STURDY Act.

Perdue’s expertise extends to industrial emissions, upholstered furniture flammability, flame retardant chemicals, formaldehyde regulation, California Proposition 65 and PFAS. He also developed AHFA’s Regulatory Toolboxes, which provide manufacturers with guidance on navigating complex compliance requirements and remain among the association’s most valued membership resources.

Jackie Hirschhaut: Strengthening Industry Connections and Engagement
Hirschhaut has played a central role in AHFA’s public relations, marketing and member engagement efforts for nearly three decades. Before joining AHFA in 1998, she served as editor-in-chief of Elegant Bride magazine and held editorial positions with Furniture Today, earning an award for excellence in trade journalism presented by the Dallas Market Center.

Early in her tenure, Hirschhaut developed a public relations program designed to educate consumers and promote interest in home furnishings and interior design. The initiative became a longstanding industrywide effort to increase consumer awareness and media coverage of home furnishings. She developed relationships with consumer media and encouraged dozens of home editors from major metropolitan newspapers to cover furniture design trends at High Point Market. She also launched AHFA's HOME Awards, recognizing outstanding writers and editors and encouraging greater coverage of home furnishings products in consumer publications.

Hirschhaut's work has helped strengthen AHFA's membership base and deepen relationships with manufacturers and industry stakeholders. Her commitment to elevating the role of public relations and marketing professionals in the home furnishings industry was also reflected in her involvement with AHFA's Marketing Conference.

She carried that commitment into her subsequent role as executive director of the International Casual Furnishings Association (ICFA), an AHFA division representing the outdoor furnishings industry. During her 11 years in that position, she initiated the association’s annual educational conference and helped enhance member programs and advance organizational initiatives.

Throughout her tenure, Hirschhaut has also overseen AHFA's Annual Meeting & CEO Conference, bringing industry leaders together to exchange ideas, address shared challenges and strengthen professional relationships.

Patricia Bowling: Informing and Advocating for the Industry
Bowling has spent more than 25 years shaping AHFA’s communications strategy and keeping furniture manufacturers informed about issues affecting their businesses. Prior to joining AHFA in 2000, she served for three years as executive vice president of the National Home Furnishings Association and spent 10 years as editor of its trade publication, then known as Home Furnishings Executive.

As vice president of communications, she has directed AHFA’s print and digital communications, including a monthly newsletter, regulatory bulletins, website content and marketing for educational programs and events. She has also served as a resource for industry media, communicating research, consumer trends and complex regulatory and product safety issues to a broader audience. Her work has helped strengthen AHFA’s ability to inform and engage its membership while advancing the association’s advocacy efforts.

Among her contributions, Bowling reintroduced and rebranded AHFA’s Marketing/PR Conference in 2024, bringing industry professionals together to explore emerging trends and strategies in marketing and communications. She also launched Furniture Safety Week, an initiative dedicated to promoting furniture safety awareness and preventing furniture tip-over incidents. Additionally, she authors AHFA’s annual Year in Review, documenting the association's accomplishments, advocacy efforts and member programs.
Through these initiatives and her longstanding relationships with industry stakeholders and the media, Bowling has helped reinforce AHFA's role as a trusted source of industry information.
